data.description: Phase A2 of the front-end design plan (docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md, board msg 283). GATED on BRANDING.md existing at repo root (Phase A1, non-Lattice, authored by designer-sofia — do not start this task before A1 ships). Deliverables: framework-neutral tokens.css (CSS custom properties) + tokens.json expressing every BRANDING.md decision (colors with contrast ratios, type scale, spacing), plus a static no-build HTML style-reference page under docs/design/style-reference/ rendering every token and primitive (button, input, table, card) in default/hover/disabled/error states. This file pair becomes the single source of visual truth for everything shipped after. Acceptance: handoff contract in plan doc section 5 — no magic values, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast recorded, semantic HTML, renders at 375px. Zero spend: open-license assets only; any license need is a board ask, not a purchase. Decision context: board directed front-end design work in #board msg 283; company brand is deliberately product-agnostic so this work is valid regardless of the step-5 outcome.
data.title: Design tokens + static style reference derived from BRANDING.md

data.body:
GATE LIFTED: BRANDING.md now exists at repo root (commit 0a50315, authored agent:designer-sofia). This task's dependency — plan A1, docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md §4 — is satisfied, so AS-29 is pullable.

Independently verified by the orchestrator before unblocking, because AS-29 encodes these numbers as tokens.css/tokens.json truth and a wrong ratio here propagates silently: all 44 contrast pairs in §3.4 were re-derived from the semantic token hex values using WCAG 2.1 relative luminance. 44/44 reproduce the documented ratio exactly, 0 below their stated threshold. Two dark-mode pairs (accent-solid, danger-solid button fills) failed Sofia's own first pass at 2.54:1 and 2.60:1 against the near-black canvas; she moved each to a lighter step in the same hue scale and recorded the correction in §3.4 rather than hiding it.

What AS-29 consumes: §3.1 primitives (ink/accent/success/warning/danger scales, hex-defined), §3.2 and §3.3 semantic aliases resolved per mode (28 tokens each, light and dark), §4.2 type scale, §6.1 spacing scale, §6.2 radius, §6.3 elevation, §6.4 breakpoints, and §6.5 which sketches a token implementation pattern. Typefaces are Inter and JetBrains Mono, both SIL OFL 1.1 with license lines recorded and verified against source.

STILL OPEN before BRANDING.md is 'adopted' per plan §4 A1: CEO and CTO both read it. Sofia announced it in #announcements (msgs 315, 316); their next inbox sweep surfaces it. That read is an acceptance step for A1, not a blocker on starting AS-29.

CTO acceptance read of BRANDING.md: ADOPTED (plan §4 A1 gate, docs/design/00-frontend-design-plan.md). Countersigned 2026-08-31; posted in full to #announcements msg 318 where Sofia announced it. Independently re-derived §3.4 with the §11 formula — all documented ratios reproduce exactly. Six findings, none blocking, all absorbed into this plan so the implementer never guesses: (F1) §4.1 'self-host fonts in-repo' contradicts §7.D.14 'no binary assets in this repository' — resolved for AS-29 as NO font binaries, fallback stacks only, no network at render time; Sofia may overrule in v1.1. (F2) §3.4 verifies foregrounds almost entirely against bg-canvas, but components sit on bg-surface/bg-surface-sunken — five dark-mode pairs fail, incl. danger-solid on bg-surface at 2.97:1 (3:1 floor), a destructive button on a card. Proved the feasible-luminance window: NON-EMPTY on bg-surface (one new danger step ~#D62937 fixes it), EMPTY on bg-surface-sunken (no colour can satisfy a 4.5:1 white label AND a 3:1 boundary — structural fix required). border-interactive/ink-500 is the one token clearing 3:1 on all three dark backgrounds (4.82/4.15/3.28) and is the structural fix. (F3) dark border-hairline is byte-identical to dark bg-surface-sunken (1.00:1) — a hairline there is absent, not subtle. (F4) no hover/active semantics outside solid fills. (F5) focus-ring geometry and border-width undefined — three allowlisted AS-29 additions. (F6) no icon set + emoji banned, so states are text+colour+shape. Palette amendments are Sofia's v1.1 call and are NOT prerequisites for this task.

Plan written and moving to planned. Approach: this task adds ZERO visual judgment — its value is fidelity and verifiability. Key decisions baked in so Sofia doesn't have to make them mid-implementation: (1) File layout — docs/design/tokens/{tokens.css,tokens.json,tokens.test.mjs} + docs/design/style-reference/{index.html,reference.css}. Tokens get their own dir because the style reference is a CONSUMER, not the owner; a future front-end app links tokens.css without reaching through a docs page. No package.json (.mjs is ESM without one; a manifest would imply a dependency surface). (2) Light/dark — four ordered blocks: primitives; light on ':root, [data-theme="light"]'; dark under '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme="light"])'; explicit '[data-theme="dark"]'. Two deliberate deltas from BRANDING §6.5: attribute selectors (not :root-only) so a nested div re-scopes the semantic layer — that is what lets the page show light AND dark side by side without touching OS settings — and color-scheme set alongside so native inputs/scrollbars follow. Blocks 3+4 duplicate 28 aliases; CSS cannot avoid that without a build step, so the test asserts they are identical. Do NOT 'DRY' it with a preprocessor. (3) tokens.json consumer contract — the parity test is the PRESENT-TENSE consumer; if the test stops reading it, delete the file. Flat, versioned, non-DTCG (considered and rejected: buys compatibility with build pipelines we have none of and have banned; revisit trigger = first real ingesting tool). Semantic tokens record BOTH resolved value and alias name — the alias is what catches 'alias says ink-700, value is ink-600'. (4) Mechanical parity — tokens.test.mjs parses BRANDING.md's own tables and compares them to both artifacts: three-way equality, completeness in BOTH directions, pinned counts (catches a row deleted from both sides), alias integrity, dark-block duplication invariant, contrast recomputation from hexes to 2dp, magic-value scan (zero raw hex outside the primitive block), mobile-first scan, and a loud failure if a table cannot be parsed. Additions are gated by an allowlist in the test file, so a fourth token requires editing a test with a reason. Consequence: BRANDING.md §3-§6 table format becomes a machine contract, same precedent as the personnel frontmatter subset in CLAUDE.md. Run with: node --test 'docs/design/tokens/*.test.mjs' — Node 22+ takes a GLOB, not a directory (verified on v24.13.1 here; node --test <dir> fails with 'Could not find').

AS-29 implementation complete on feat/AS-29-design-tokens (3 commits: 03180fb tokens.css+json, f4e6b52 style reference, d3fc751 tokens.test.mjs).

BUILT: docs/design/tokens/{tokens.css,tokens.json,tokens.test.mjs}, docs/design/style-reference/{index.html,reference.css}. No package.json, zero deps, opens from file://.

TEST RESULTS (real numbers, `node --test 'docs/design/tokens/*.test.mjs'` from repo root): 28/28 pass, 0 fail. 54/54 §3.4 rows recompute to the documented ratio at 2dp with zero mismatches (tokens.css is byte-accurate against BRANDING.md). 114-row generated matrix (19 fg x 3 bg x 2 modes) written to tokens.json.contrast as a side effect. Dark-block duplication invariant confirmed. Alias integrity confirmed including the focus-ring semantic-to-semantic case.

F2/F3 DECISION: did not amend BRANDING.md — implemented against the current palette, taking your plan's own stated default (§11 open question #2). Reasoning: (1) your structural resolution (border-interactive boundary on sunken, honest labeling elsewhere) already fully satisfies AS-29's acceptance criteria with zero palette change — that's why you designed it that way; (2) BRANDING.md shipped as v1 at time-box, and a narrow single-hex tweak mid-AS-29 is the over-polish failure mode my own dossier names, not a considered v1.1 pass; (3) the proposed #D62937 only fixes 1 of the fails that exist — the bg-surface-sunken fails are structurally unfixable by any color (empty feasible window, already proven), so a partial fix leaves the palette half-addressed, worse than either shipping honest or doing v1.1 properly later.

NEW FINDING beyond the 3 named in msg 318: the generated matrix (mechanical, all 114 combos) found 12 real fails, not 3 — all dark mode. Named: danger-solid/bg-surface 2.97, accent-solid/bg-surface-sunken 2.70, danger-solid/bg-surface-sunken 2.35. Not previously named: accent-solid-hover on canvas/surface/sunken (2.54/2.19/1.73), danger-solid-hover on canvas/surface/sunken (2.60/2.24/1.77), focus-ring on sunken (2.70 — same token as accent-solid in dark mode), danger-text and danger-text-on-subtle on sunken (4.28, just under the 4.5 text floor — this one is actually already in your plan's F2 prose, just not the "3 numbers" list). None fixed here, same reasoning as above; all 12 render honestly labeled in the style reference's contrast-matrix section, and the two you flagged carry inline ratio badges on the destructive-button demos. This is what §8.3's "enumeration problem stops being a diligence problem" was for — input for your v1.1 pass.

PARSER FAIL-LOUD PROOF (manual, against the real file, not committed): (1) corrupted the §3.2 heading text -> "FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in BRANDING.md §3.1: found start marker... but not end marker..."; whole suite failed, 0 pass, not a silent skip. (2) corrupted the ink table's first data row (dropped the --color- prefix) -> "FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in BRANDING.md §3.1: expected to find a table for 'ink primitives' but none matched." Restored via backup both times, confirmed byte-identical + git-clean, 28/28 green again after each.

RENDERING VERIFICATION (real, not assumed): installed Playwright in my scratchpad (not part of the shipped tree) and drove the actual file:// page in real Chromium. Confirmed: body bg/color resolve to the exact documented hex in both light and dark OS-preference emulation; a primitive swatch's rendered background matches its documented hex exactly; primary button fill/radius/padding match §7 exactly; a nested data-theme="light" panel correctly overrides an inherited dark page and vice versa (the block 2/3/4 specificity design actually works); dark theming works with JS disabled; zero console/page errors throughout.

Caught and fixed two real bugs this way: (1) real horizontal overflow at 375px (523px content in a 375px viewport) — the wordmark's inline SVG had no max-width, forcing ancestor flex/grid containers wider than the viewport (CSS min-width:auto blowout); fixed with max-width:100% on the SVG + min-width:0 on the panels, re-verified scrollWidth==clientWidth==375 exactly. (2) a real hole in my own test: the magic-value scanner's extraction logic silently produced an empty string for a plain .css file (no <style> tags to extract from), so reference.css was never actually checked — passed only because there was nothing to check. Exactly the AS-17/AS-26 failure mode this suite exists to prevent, found in its own harness. Fixed, and the corrected scanner then found (and I fixed) an invented 1px/2px/0.15em/0.2em link-hover treatment with no token backing — redesigned to reuse border-width-hairline/focus-ring-width rather than invent a 4th/5th addition.

Also implemented BRANDING.md §5.1 details not yet in my first draft: the wordmark's specified break point ("THE AMERICAN"/"SOFTWARE COMPANY" via non-breaking-space word-gluing) and the sub-480px tracking reduction to 0.04em (a literal from BRANDING's own prose, not invented — allowlisted by name in the test alongside the wordmark SVG's 1.5em illustrative sizing).

NOT VERIFIED: cross-browser rendering (Chromium only), print styles (none specified/built), assistive-tech pass beyond semantic HTML + the SVG's aria-label.

DEVIATIONS: none substantive. Two implementer-discretion additions, both "compositions not new brand values": overflow-x:auto wrappers on the type-scale/breakpoints/contrast tables (extending the pattern you specified for the component table, since those are also wide); min-width:0 on grid/flex containers (CSS-correctness fix, not visual). tokens.json gained one schema key beyond your illustrative example (scale.font-family) to hold the §4.1 stacks, since your example didn't enumerate a slot for them but they need to live in tokens.json to mirror tokens.css as you specified.

Not transitioning status, not merging, not pushing — leaving that to you.

QA REVIEW — AS-29 (cold, no implementer context). VERDICT: FAIL — implementation-level rework needed.

Reviewed on feat/AS-29-design-tokens @ d3fc751 in .worktrees/AS-29. Diff is 5 added files, 3999 insertions, no package.json, no lockfile, no binaries. Worktree clean before and after every experiment below; every mutation restored and re-checksummed byte-identical (sha256).

WHAT IS CORRECT. The artifacts themselves are right, and I checked that by hand rather than trusting the suite. Suite: 28 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail, real (node --test 'docs/design/tokens/*.test.mjs', v24.13.1); 54 §3.4 rows (27 light + 27 dark) recompute to the documented ratio at 2dp; running it leaves the tree clean (the tokens.json.contrast write is genuinely idempotent). Render: driven in real headless Chrome over CDP with DNS hard-failed (--host-resolver-rules="MAP * ~NOTFOUND"), isolated --user-data-dir, port 9334 — exactly 3 network requests, all file:// (index.html, tokens.css, reference.css), 0 failed loads, 0 console errors, 132 CSS rules live, 20502 chars rendered. No @font-face; the only http:// strings in the tree are the two SVG xmlns namespace identifiers, which are never fetched. 375px: document scrollWidth === clientWidth === 375; 54 elements exceed the viewport and all 54 sit inside div.type-scale-table-wrap / div.table-demo-wrap overflow-x containers — zero uncontained; widest section-level box is exactly 343px. Light and dark both render on one page (3 + 3 data-theme wrappers), nested override works in a real cascade in both directions, and with Emulation.setScriptExecutionDisabled the body still resolves to rgb(248,248,250) / rgb(18,21,25) under each prefers-color-scheme — criterion 4 holds with JS off. Components: 4 button variants in base/hover, focus shown statically, disabled via the real attribute; inputs with labels, aria-describedby, aria-invalid error state, disabled attribute; table row-hover static, numeric column in mono; 3 sunken cards for the F3 demo. F4 link hover changes text-decoration-thickness only, reusing --focus-ring-width — no colour change, no 4th token. F1 disclosure is present and better than asked: it names the fallback stack AND reports which faces were detected locally. Exactly 3 AS-29 additions. 16 refusals rendered.

CONTRAST HONESTY (criterion 10) — SATISFIED. I parsed all 114 rendered rows out of index.html and diffed them against the generated tokens.json.contrast: 114/114 match on ratio, threshold and result, with zero rows hidden and zero rows claiming PASS where the matrix says FAIL. All 12 generated FAILs (12 dark, 0 light) are rendered and badged FAIL, including the four the CTO never named by number (accent-solid-hover 2.54/2.19/1.73, danger-solid-hover 2.60/2.24/1.77, focus-ring-on-sunken 2.70, danger-text/-on-subtle 4.28). Sofia's 12 is right and nothing lies about AA. Caveat below.

I ALSO VERIFIED, BY HAND, 201 FACTS THE SUITE NEVER CHECKS — all correct: tokens.json.primitive.color (43 hexes) vs BRANDING §3.1; all 56 semantic .alias fields vs the "Alias of" column, plus alias->hex closure; additions parity json<->css; $meta.sourceCommit "0a50315" is genuinely BRANDING.md's commit; 99 swatch hex text labels (43 primitive + 56 semantic) and the 100th (#2F3441 in the F3 prose) all correct.

=== WHY THIS FAILS: the suite is weaker than the plan says it is ===

Primary brief was to hunt for assertions that pass while the property they check is false. I found eight. Method: mutate one file, run the suite, restore, re-checksum. Every "NOT CAUGHT" below left the suite at 28/28 green.

BLOCKING — each maps to a stated §8.1 assertion or acceptance criterion:

V1. §8.1.2 "completeness, BOTH directions" is implemented for tokens.css block 1 only. Blocks 2/3/4 have no "nothing extra" check.
  - added `--color-smuggled-brand-value: #BADA55;` to block 2 -> NOT CAUGHT.
  - added `--sneaky-radius: 13px;` to block 2 -> NOT CAUGHT.
  - added `--sneaky-dark-radius: 13px;` to BOTH dark blocks -> NOT CAUGHT (the duplication invariant filters on the `color-` prefix, so non-colour tokens are invisible to it; a 29th *colour* token in both dark blocks IS caught by the 28 count pin, and one in block 4 alone is caught by the key-set diff — block 2 has neither guard).
  Consequence: plan §4.4 calls the ADDITIONS allowlist "the mechanism that keeps 'additions' from becoming a back door for undocumented brand values." The back door is open — declare the 4th token one block lower and no test objects. This is the single most important fix.

V2. §8.1.1 three-way equality omits §3.1 primitives in tokens.json. Nothing in tokens.test.mjs ever reads `tokensJson.primitive` (grep confirms: only .semantic, .scale, .additions, .contrast).
  - corrupted primitive.color["ink-50"] to #FF00FF -> NOT CAUGHT.
  - deleted the entire `primitive` key (all 43 values) -> NOT CAUGHT.
  Criterion 3 requires every §3.1 token present in BOTH artifacts; for tokens.json that is currently unenforced.

V3. The magic-value scanner's non-empty guard exists on the HTML branch only. `if (kind === 'css') cssLike = text;` has no `assert.ok(cssLike.length > 0)`; the else branch does.
  - truncated reference.css to zero bytes -> NOT CAUGHT, 28/28 green, page renders completely unstyled.
  This is the exact bug Sofia found and fixed in this same function, left asymmetric in the fix. It is the 4th instance of the AS-17/AS-26 class, and the test file's own header declares this principle non-negotiable.

V4. §8.1.6's threshold clause and the whole §8.3 "documented PASS still passes" test silently disable if BRANDING's Result cell carries any decoration, because `resultCell.split(/\s|—/)[0]` takes the first whitespace-delimited word.
  - positive control: `| 14.85:1 | 99:1 | PASS |` (PASS claimed at an unreachable floor) -> CAUGHT, good.
  - same row as `| 14.85:1 | 99:1 | OK PASS |` -> NOT CAUGHT.
  - realistic drift `| ✅ PASS |` across the whole table -> NOT CAUGHT.
  When it degrades, the §8.3 test executes zero assertions and still reports green — there is no floor asserting how many PASS rows were actually examined. A brand doc that adds a tick emoji to its own table silently switches off its AA enforcement.

NON-BLOCKING (worth backlog tasks; I am not blocking `done` on these):

B1. tokens.json's 56 `alias` fields are never read by any test — I replaced every one with "WRONG-ALIAS" and got 28/28 green. Plan §5 names that column as "what makes the parity check meaningful (it catches 'alias says ink-700, value is ink-600')"; today it is decorative. Correct on disk; unguarded.
B2. The page's 100 hex text labels and 114 hand-transcribed matrix rows have no join to the generated data. I changed a swatch label to #BADA55, changed a printed ratio to 99.99:1, relabelled the dark danger-solid/bg-surface FAIL as PASS, and deleted a FAIL row outright — all four NOT CAUGHT. Criterion 10 is met today because Sofia transcribed honestly, not because anything enforces it. Highest-consequence drift path in the deliverable and cheap to close (the generated matrix and the page are both in-repo).
B3. Further magic-value scanner blind spots, all latent — I confirmed none occur in the shipped files: declarations with no trailing semicolon escape `declRe` entirely (`padding-top: 13px` is caught with `;`, not caught without); SVG presentation attributes are outside the scanned CSS context (`<svg fill="#FF0000">` -> green; the two shipped SVGs correctly use `fill="currentColor"`); units other than px/rem/em are unscanned (`7vw` -> green); a one-off `@media (min-width: 700px)` with no naming comment is explicitly skipped; and rewriting a named breakpoint in range syntax `(width >= 480px)` drops its comment requirement -> green. The @media-comment test also has no floor on how many queries it inspected.
B4. `color-scheme` is required by plan §4.1 in three places and asserted nowhere — removing it from block 4 -> green. Correct on disk.
B5. btn-ghost has no disabled variant on the page (the other 3 variants do); plan §7 says "Disabled (any button)". Cosmetic gap in the demo, not the tokens.

FAIL-LOUD GUARD (§8.1.9 / criterion 1) — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, PASSES. Not taking Sofia's word:
  - corrupted the §3.2 heading -> whole suite aborts, 0 pass / 1 fail: "FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in BRANDING.md §3.2: could not find start marker ... this is a hard failure, not a skip."
  - corrupted the ink table's first data row (dropped the --color- prefix) -> aborts, 0 pass: 'expected to find a table for "ink primitives" but none matched.'
  - deleted a §3.2 semantic row -> aborts: 'Cannot resolve "text-muted" in light mode'.
  - changed one BRANDING hex -> CAUGHT by alias integrity. Changed one documented ratio without touching a hex -> CAUGHT by recomputation.
  All four restored byte-identical (sha256 verified each time); 28/28 green after each restore. The guard fails by name, not silently.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (plan §9) ===
1 partial — suite passes and all 9 §8.1 assertions exist by name, §8.1.9 demonstrably fails loudly; but §8.1.1, §8.1.2, §8.1.6/§8.3 and §8.1.7 are incompletely realised (V1–V4).
2 PASS — file://, no server, no network (DNS hard-failed), renders completely, 0 console errors.
3 PASS on disk, partial in enforcement — every token present and rendered; verified by hand, since V2 means the suite would not notice a missing tokens.json primitive block.
4 PASS — both themes on one page, nested override real, correct with JS disabled.
5 partial — no magic value exists in the shipped files (verified by hand); the scan that is supposed to guarantee that has V3/B3 holes, and a raw hex substituted for a block-2 var() alias in tokens.css also goes green (same value -> unnoticed; different value -> caught).
6 PASS.  7 PASS (scrollWidth === clientWidth === 375, nothing uncontained, 343px content).  8 PASS.  9 PASS (exactly 3, each allowlisted with a reason).  10 PASS on the page; unenforced (B2).

NO INLINE FIXES APPLIED. Every finding changes what the suite enforces, which is behavioural, not trivia — and a reviewer verifying her own patch is the conflict this gate exists to prevent. Nothing was committed to the branch; the worktree is exactly as I found it.

RECOMMENDED REWORK SCOPE (implementation-level, all inside tokens.test.mjs): (1) extend the "nothing extra" check to blocks 2/3/4, colour and non-colour; (2) assert tokens.json.primitive against BRANDING §3.1 both directions; (3) hoist the non-empty guard so it covers the css branch, and assert a minimum row/query count in the §8.3 and @media tests so they cannot report green on zero assertions; (4) parse the Result cell strictly (exact match on PASS/FAIL/EXEMPT/DECORATIVE, fail loudly on anything else) instead of taking the first word. B1–B5 are backlog, not gates.

The plan is sound and needs no rework — §8.1 specifies the right assertions. This is a gap between what §8 promises and what the file enforces, on a task whose stated entire value is fidelity and verifiability. Route review -> in_progress.

Reproduction: harnesses are in my scratchpad and are not part of the tree — mutate.mjs (28 cases, snapshot/mutate/run/restore/re-checksum), verify-unchecked.mjs, verify-page.mjs, render-check.mjs, render-check2.mjs. Chrome ran headless on ports 9333/9334 with a throwaway profile, both killed and profiles removed; asc-chat-server-1 on 8347 was never touched and is still up and healthy.

AS-29 cycle-2 rework complete on feat/AS-29-design-tokens @ bf8996f. Implemented by agent:developer-marcus (task stays assigned to agent:designer-sofia — this cycle was test-harness engineering with no visual judgment). ONE file changed: docs/design/tokens/tokens.test.mjs, +490/-28. Zero changes to tokens.css, tokens.json, index.html or reference.css — Priya hand-verified 201 facts in cycle 1 with zero mismatches, so the artifacts are right and I did not touch them.

TEST COUNTS: 28/28 pass before, 35/35 pass after. Tree clean after every run (the tokens.json.contrast write is still idempotent).

METHOD, and the standard I held myself to: for every assertion I touched or added, mutate the thing it claims to check, run the suite, restore, re-checksum all five artifacts with sha256. A fix I cannot demonstrate failing is not a fix. 33 mutation cases; ALL 33 now CAUGHT, against 22 that were green before this commit. Every restore verified byte-identical. I also confirmed each mutation is caught by the assertion written for it, not incidentally by an unrelated one.

=== THE FOUR BLOCKING FIXES, WITH PROOF ===

V1 — additions gate scanned block 1 only. Blocks 2/3/4 now assert their declared custom-property set EQUALS BRANDING.md's semantic set exactly (deepEqual on sorted keys, so extra and missing both fail); allowlisted additions are permitted in any block, which is what the allowlist is for. The dark-block duplication invariant no longer filters on the 'color-' prefix and now compares raw declaration text as well as resolved values (plan §4.2 asks for identical content, not merely identical resolution).
  - '--color-smuggled-brand-value: #BADA55' in block 2 -> was green, now CAUGHT by the new blocks-2/3/4 completeness test.
  - '--sneaky-radius: 13px' in block 2 -> was green, now CAUGHT by the same test.
  - '--sneaky-dark-radius: 13px' in BOTH dark blocks -> was green, now CAUGHT by BOTH the duplication invariant and the completeness test.
  - '--color-smuggled-dark' in block 4 only -> was already caught by the key-set diff; still caught, now by two tests.

V2 — tokens.json.primitive read by nothing. Now asserted both directions, count pinned at 43, with tokens.css block 1 checked as the third leg of §8.1.1.
  - corrupt primitive.color['ink-50'] to #FF00FF -> was green, now CAUGHT.
  - delete the entire 'primitive' key (all 43) -> was green, now CAUGHT.
  - add an undocumented 'ink-42' to tokens.json -> was green, now CAUGHT (nothing-extra direction).

V3 — non-empty guard covered the HTML branch only. Hoisted so it covers both, plus module-level byte floors on all four parsed files and a per-file declaration floor inside the scan (index.html parses 141 declarations today, reference.css 386; floors are 100 and 300).
  - truncate reference.css to zero bytes -> was green, now CAUGHT and it aborts the whole suite by name: 'FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in docs/design/style-reference/reference.css: file is 0 bytes, below the 8000-byte floor.'
  - gut reference.css to one valid rule -> CAUGHT.
  - pad reference.css past the byte floor but leave one rule -> CAUGHT by the declaration floor, independently of the byte floor.
  - strip every inline style attribute from index.html -> CAUGHT by the declaration floor.

V4 — Result cell parsed as split(/\s|—/)[0]. Now strict: exactly PASS/FAIL/EXEMPT/DECORATIVE, optionally followed by ' — <rationale>' (how §3.4 writes its EXEMPT/DECORATIVE rows today); anything else is a named FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN abort. Added floors so the AA tests cannot run zero assertions: 54 rows recomputed, 50 PASS thresholds checked, 34 documented PASS rows compared against the generated matrix. Also made a PASS row with a non-numeric threshold, and a non-numeric ratio, hard parse errors.
  - positive control '| 14.85:1 | 99:1 | PASS |' -> still CAUGHT.
  - same row as '| OK PASS |' -> was green, now aborts by name.
  - '| ✅ PASS |' across the whole table -> was green, now aborts: 'FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in BRANDING.md §3.4 light: Result cell \"✅ PASS\" for pair \"text-primary on bg-canvas\" is not one of PASS / FAIL / EXEMPT / DECORATIVE...'
  - added a unit guard test exercising parseResultCell against OK PASS, ✅ PASS, PASSES, pass, 'PASS (probably)' and ''.

=== ALSO HARDENED (backlog items I judged cheap, safe and high-value) ===

B1 alias fields — all 56 tokens.json 'alias' values now read and compared to BRANDING's 'Alias of' column, plus alias->hex closure and a nothing-extra check. Replacing every alias with 'WRONG-ALIAS' was green, now CAUGHT; so is a single alias swapped ink-700 -> ink-600. Plan §5 names this column as exactly what makes parity meaningful, so it had to be read.

B4 color-scheme — asserted in all three semantic blocks. Removing it from block 4 was green, now CAUGHT. NOTE A DEVIATION I DID NOT 'FIX': plan §4.1 specifies ':root { color-scheme: light dark }' but Sofia shipped ':root, [data-theme=\"light\"] { color-scheme: light }' with block 3 supplying dark under prefers-color-scheme. ## 3. Did the hardening introduce vacuous passes of its own?

I applied the same standard to Marcus's 490 new lines. **No new blocking vacuous pass.** Two of my initial eight suspects were my own harness misfiring and I withdraw them: index.html has ZERO `<style>` blocks (all 141 declarations come from 132 inline `style=""` attributes), so my "empty the style block" and "multi-line declaration in a style block" cases mutated nothing. Multi-line values are in fact parsed correctly — `\s*` after the colon consumes the newline — and I confirmed that with a real multi-line magic value in reference.css, which was caught.

What genuinely remains green (all BACKLOG, none violating a stated criterion):

R1 — **Selectors are never verified. This is the largest remaining hole, and it is MY miss from cycle 1, not a regression.** The parsers slice blocks by banner comment and read declarations regardless of which rule they sit in. I changed block 4's selector from `[data-theme="dark"]` to `.bogus4`, rendered the page in headless Chrome, and all six theme panels came back light (`--color-bg-canvas: #F8F8FA`, `color-scheme: light`) — acceptance criterion 4 completely broken — with the suite at **35/35 green**. Same for block 2's selector. Not blocking: plan §8.1 enumerates nine assertions and selector verification is not among them; the shipped artifact satisfies criterion 4 (re-verified on the byte-identical file: 6 panels, correct light/dark tokens, correct per-panel `color-scheme`, 3 file:// requests, zero network).

R2 — Same family, new code: `parsePlainDeclarations(block2Text)['color-scheme']` matches anywhere in the block's TEXT RANGE, not on the block's rule. I moved `color-scheme: light` into a decoy rule inside block 2 and the test stayed green while the real `:root, [data-theme="light"]` rule had none. The assertion is named "declared alongside every semantic block"; it verifies "the string appears somewhere between two banner comments."

R3 — The page's PAINT is not joined to its labels. Labels are now airtight, but `style="background:var(--color-accent-600)"` on a swatch chip can be repointed at `--color-danger-600`, or deleted entirely, and the suite stays green.

R4 — `themeAt()` is a textual last-mention scan, not an ancestor check. A dark swatch moved outside every panel but positioned after the last dark panel still validates as "dark". The assertion claims to detect "sits outside any data-theme panel"; it cannot.

R5 — §3.4's own threshold column is trusted. Lowering a documented `4.5:1` to `1.0:1` keeps the row PASSing. Implemented exactly as plan §8.1.6 words it ("clear its stated threshold"), so this is a plan-text limit, not an implementation defect. Cheap fix available: cross-check §3.4's stated threshold against the generated matrix's kind-derived floor, which already applies real WCAG values.

R6 — Pre-existing from cycle 1, not introduced here: the magic-value scan exempts breakpoint values and `375` by VALUE GLOBALLY, not by context. `padding-top: 768px` and `padding-top: 375px` both pass, though the comments describe media-query and demo-box contexts. Plan §8.1.7 scopes the allowlist to `@media` literals; the code is looser than the plan text.

R7 — `:root { color-scheme: light dark }` in block 1 is inert: block 2 unconditionally overrides `:root` with `color-scheme: light`. Deleting it changes nothing rendered and nothing asserted. Harmless, but misleading to the next editor.

Floors, measured against reality: index.html 141 declarations (floor 100), reference.css 386 (floor 300), media queries 10 (floor 8), byte floors well under actual. Loose, but the value/label joins are the real check and those are tight.

## 7. Is the machine contract too brittle for Sofia to maintain her own doc?

**The balance is right, with one caveat worth acting on.** My read, having deliberately tried to break it: every strictness I hit failed LOUDLY and BY NAME — `FORMAT CONTRACT BROKEN in BRANDING.md §3.4 light: Result cell "✅ PASS" for pair "text-primary on bg-canvas" is not one of PASS / FAIL / EXEMPT / DECORATIVE`. That is a good error. It tells the author what she typed, where, and what the four legal values are. A contract that fails like that is maintainable; one that fails with `expected 54 to equal 0` is not, and this is emphatically the former.

The strictness is also load-bearing rather than decorative: the decorated-Result-cell case is exactly how §3.4 silently stopped enforcing AA in cycle 1. Loosening the parser to tolerate `✅ PASS` would re-open the defect this cycle was convened to close. Adding a §3.4 row is not blocked at all — the pinned count is the intended tripwire, and updating `27` to `28` in the same commit is the correct workflow and is what §8.4 already tells her.

The caveat: the contract is now documented in the plan (§8.4) and in the test file, but **not in BRANDING.md itself**, which is where its author works. §8.4 says to record it in BRANDING.md §0 as part of the v1.1 amendment; that has not happened, and employees cannot edit BRANDING.md under this task's scope anyway. Until it does, Sofia's first encounter with the contract will be a red build rather than a note in her own document. That is a real maintainability gap and I have written it up as R8 below rather than as a blocker, because it is a BRANDING.md edit and this task explicitly excludes those (plan §10).
